nodes.label: Infrared Night-Mode Frame (Siren, 2022-02-22 08:14:11)
nodes.description: Monochrome (infrared night-vision) overhead still labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-02-22 08:14:11'. The scene is entirely greyscale: the normally red feeder caps appear dark grey and the litter is a mottled grey field. Birds are small young chicks scattered sparsely, with clear bare floor between most individuals and loose rings around the feeders. Motion blur on several chicks indicates a long exposure under low light.

nodes.label: Greyscale IR vs Colour Domain Shift
nodes.description: The same camera switches automatically between colour daylight capture and monochrome infrared capture, so the dataset contains two visually distinct imaging domains of one physical scene.
nodes.rationale: Any pipeline that relies on colour cues - for example locating the bright red feeder caps to anchor the feeding zone, or separating white birds from grey litter by saturation - silently loses that cue on IR frames. The practical consequences are that anchors must be geometric rather than chromatic, and that colour-jitter or grayscale augmentation is needed so a single model covers both domains instead of training two.

nodes.label: Early Growth Stage Flock
nodes.description: The earliest-dated observation in this chunk (22 February): small chicks occupying only a fraction of the floor area, well separated, giving the cleanest instance separation of any frame here. Apparent bird size in pixels is therefore a proxy for age within the production cycle.
